title: American Rye
subtitle: 1790s to now
description: How rye became the whiskey of Pennsylvania and Maryland, nearly disappeared after Prohibition, and came back with whiskey made in Kentucky and Indiana. Four pours.

pours.name: Old Overholt
pours.notes: A Pennsylvania name, made in Kentucky. Beam does not publish the recipe.

pours.name: Pikesville Straight Rye
pours.notes: Reported to be 51% rye, the legal minimum. Six years old and 110 proof. Try it neat, then with water.

pours.name: Old Forester Rye
pours.notes: 65% rye, 20% malted barley, 15% corn, as Brown-Forman publishes it. Compare it with the Pikesville.

pours.name: Bulleit 95 Rye
pours.notes: 95% rye, distilled in Indiana. Find that on the back label, then taste it against the Pikesville.
